title: Day 2 · everything Verne wrote about the next three days
learning_goal: Know who Fogg is, what he bet, and that the whole crossing of Europe exists in the novel as seven timestamps; feel the size of the gap we are about to walk into.

narration.script:
Day two. If you have just joined us: in 1872 Jules Verne published a novel. A London gentleman named Phileas Fogg bets half his money that he can travel round the world in eighty days. He left London last night at a quarter to nine, with a French servant, Passepartout.

The route was printed in the newspaper on the night of the bet. The first line says: 'London to Suez, by way of Mont Cenis and Brindisi, by rail and steamboats — seven days.'

That is nearly all the novel says. Fogg keeps a notebook. The first line: 'Left London, Wednesday, October the second, at eight forty-five p.m.'

The last line: 'Sailed on the Mongolia, Saturday, at five p.m.'

Seven lines. Three thousand kilometres.
